headline: Benchmarks of sequencing read processing and profiling tools across microbial genomics
label: Genomic Sequencing Tool Benchmarks
summary: Recent preprints benchmark nanopore trimming, viral detection, and k-mer profilers, while a 2026 SRA snapshot shows sparse protocol annotation.
synthesis: The dominant thread is benchmarking and methodological correction of inference from microbial sequencing data. Several items quantify tool performance under controlled or simulated conditions: nanopore trimming and quality-filtering pipelines on 13 bacterial isolates, eleven viral prediction tools on low-abundance metagenomes, and KMA and Kallisto k-mer profilers whose relative abundance estimates are biased by sample-reference distance and similar references. Others propose corrections or new tools, including DeepMM for splitting chimeric contigs before binning and Metalink for joint taxonomic and functional profiling, which is reported to outperform HUMAnN3. Nanopore rRNA operon sequencing, with error rates below ~0.008, is presented as enabling strain-level quantification. Reporting quality also appears as a concern, since protocol keyword coverage in the Sequence Read Archive fell to 1.42% between the 2015 analysis and the 2026 snapshot.
